## What I did

The spec (`.docs/instructions.md`) is the exercism "markdown" refactoring exercise: rewrite the confusing parser in `markdown.go` to be easier to read and maintain while keeping all tests green. I only touched `markdown.go` — `markdown_test.go` and `cases_test.go` are unchanged, and no new files were created.

**Before:** `Render` was a single byte-at-a-time loop threading five ad-hoc flags (`header`, `list`, `listOpened`, `he`, `pos`) through tangled branches, with emphasis done via four global `strings.Replace` calls up front.

**After:** a line-based approach that matches how markdown is actually structured:

- `Render` splits the input on `\n` and renders each line as one of three things — a header, a list item, or a paragraph — tracking only a single `inList` boolean to open/close the `<ul>`.
- `applyEmphasis` extracts the bold/italic conversion (kept as the same four `Replace` calls so behavior is preserved exactly).
- `isListItem` / `listItemContent` handle the `* ` prefix.
- `renderLine` + `headerLevel` handle headers: 1–6 leading `#` followed by a space is a header; seven or more hashes falls through to a paragraph.

I added comments explaining the refactor rationale, as the spec suggested. The old code's subtle behaviors are all preserved — e.g. a `#`/`*` appearing mid-line is treated as literal text, and a `*` inside an already-open list item is literal text — because the line-based logic only interprets symbols at the start of a line.
